title: Immunohistochemistry and High Resolution Microscopy of Rat Gastric Enteroendocrine Cells
author: Billie Hunne
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xeyfjfw
materials: Cryosections (12 μm) were cut onto Superfrost Plus microscope slides (Menzel-Glaser; Thermo Fisher, Scoresby, VIC, Australia), air dried for 1 hour and then blocked in a solution of 10% normal horse serum with 1% Triton-X100 in PBS for 30 min at room temperature. Mixtures of up to 3 primary antibodies from different species were diluted and applied to slides overnight at 4°C. Slides were washed with 3 changes of PBS and then incubated with an appropriate mixture of Alexa fluor labelled secondary antibodies for 90 min at room temperature. After a further 3 changes of PBS, coverslips were applied with Dako fluorescence mounting medium (Agilent, Tullamarine, VIC, Australia). Samples for which the primary antibodies were omitted were analysed to investigate background staining and autofluorescence and were used to set appropriate thresholds for quantification.

steps.title: Prepare animals
steps.instruction: Select Sprague‑Dawley rats weighing 250–350 g and provide food and water ad libitum before experiments.

substeps.instruction: Provide food and water ad libitum prior to the experiments.

steps.title: Anesthetize rats
steps.instruction: Inject a ketamine/xylazine mixture (55 mg/kg ketamine, 9 mg/kg xylazine) to achieve surgical anaesthesia.

steps.title: Perfuse with PBS and fixative
steps.instruction: Perform transcardial perfusion first with heparinised PBS (0.15 M NaCl, 0.01 M sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.2) then with fixative (2 % formaldehyde, 0.2 % picric acid in 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0).

substeps.instruction: Transcardially perfuse with heparinised PBS (0.15 M NaCl, 0.01 M sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.2).
Immediately follow with fixative (2 % formaldehyde, 0.2 % picric acid in 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0).

steps.title: Dissect and post‑fix stomach
steps.instruction: Remove the stomach, dissect it, and post‑fix overnight at 4 °C in the same fixative solution.

steps.title: Clear tissue
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue three times for 10 min each in dimethyl sulfoxide, then three times for 10 min each in PBS.

steps.title: Store in sucrose‑azide
steps.instruction: Transfer tissue to PBS‑sucrose‑azide (30 % sucrose, 0.1 % sodium azide in PBS) and keep at 4 °C.

steps.title: Equilibrate in OCT
steps.instruction: Incubate tissue overnight at 4 °C in a 1:1 mixture of PBS‑sucrose‑azide and OCT compound (Tissue Tek, Elkhart, IN, USA).

steps.title: Embed and freeze
steps.instruction: Embed the equilibrated tissue in OCT compound and freeze for sectioning.

steps.title: Collect sections
steps.instruction: Obtain sections from the antrum and corpus of the stomach; tissue from 4 animals will be analysed.

steps.title: Image sections for cell counts
steps.instruction: Acquire tile‑scan images with a nominal optical thickness of 7.7 μm using a 10× objective on a Zeiss LSM800 confocal microscope, selecting a 1.5 mm‑wide region that spans the full mucosal thickness.

substeps.instruction: Acquire tile scans (optical thickness 7.7 μm) with 10× objective on LSM800.
Select a 1.5 mm‑wide region containing the full thickness of the mucosa.

steps.title: Convert images for analysis
steps.instruction: Save each separate channel and the merged image as TIFF files, open them in Fiji, convert to greyscale, and input the pixel scale from the microscope metadata.

substeps.instruction: Save each channel and merged image as TIFF.
Open in Fiji, convert to greyscale, and set pixel scale using microscope metadata.

steps.title: Count positive cells
steps.instruction: Manually circle cells; count a cell as positive if its mean grey intensity exceeds a threshold set from negative‑control images, then measure total mucosal area to calculate density (positive cells / mm²) and record numbers in the top versus bottom half of the mucosa.

substeps.instruction: Manually circle cells in each channel.
Mark a cell as positive when its mean grey value is above the threshold derived from negative‑control images.
Measure total mucosal area to compute cell density (positive cells per mm²).
Determine the number of positive cells in the top half and bottom half of the mucosa.
